investigator.method:
Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (INSUFFICIENT) then Level 2 STRUCTURAL (SUFFICIENT). All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion). Level 1: curl GETs of https://www.coliseu.pt, /agenda, and a candidate /evento/:slug detail route all returned byte-identical, empty client-rendered shells (
, no JSON-LD, no server-rendered event data) — independently re-confirming the prior loose note in sources/porto.json. Level 2: the same public page's own /env-config.js (also fetched via curl) exposes a GRAPHQL_API config value; the referenced GraphQL endpoint (https://nest.coliseu.pt/graph/) was probed with plain, read-only, non-mutating GraphQL queries (a __typename liveness check, then standard GraphQL introspection of the query schema and the Event/Room types, then a bounded 5-event sample query, then two eventBySlug lookups to empirically cross-check id stability, then a direct GET of a client route pattern found in the retained JS bundle). All of these are ordinary read-only GraphQL-over-HTTP requests to a publicly CORS-open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) endpoint already referenced by the site's own public client code — not a private/internal API, not authentication bypass, not brute force. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed every retained evidence file deterministically to cross-check all claims below. Level 2 was SUFFICIENT; no browser/headless session (Level 3) was ever opened.

probe_history.reason:
Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://www.coliseu.pt, https://www.coliseu.pt/agenda, and https://www.coliseu.pt/evento/20260912-he-s-back-michael-jackson-tribute all returned 200 OK with byte-identical 3,817-byte HTML bodies: a bare `` shell whose entire visible body is `
` plus loader/vendor `

Inspecting the same public page's own referenced assets (per Level 2 guidance: public JS/bootstrap data and publicly-referenced endpoints) found /env-config.js — itself served publicly at https://www.coliseu.pt/env-config.js — declaring `GRAPHQL_API: "https://nest.coliseu.pt/graph/"`. A plain GET to that endpoint returned `400 Bad Request` with body `"GET query missing."` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, i.e. a live, public, CORS-open GraphQL server documenting its own expected protocol. A minimal read-only `{__typename}` query returned `{"data":{"__typename":"Query"}}`; standard GraphQL introspection (also read-only, not a mutation, not credentialed) then revealed a full public query schema including `events`/`eventBySlug` and an `Event` type with id/name/startDate/slug/category/room/promoter/ticketsUrl/estimatedDuration fields, but no price/cost field anywhere in the 179-type schema. A bounded 5-event sample query (paging limit 5, isVisible:true, isArchived:false, sorted by startDate ascending) returned totalCount 72 and 5 fully-populated event records with genuine UTC ISO `startDate` instants. Two of those five ids were independently cross-checked via a separate `eventBySlug` query path and reproduced identically (2/2), satisfying the stable-identifier rule empirically. The retained main JS bundle was also confirmed (via the offline-proof script) to literally contain the React route pattern `/evento/:slug`, and a direct curl GET of that constructed URL for one sampled event's slug resolved 200 OK (not 404). This already fully answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment without needing any JS execution or browser session, so escalation to Level 3 (BROWSER_OBSERVATION) was not attempted.

venue_reference: Coliseu Porto Ageas — R. de Passos Manuel 137, 4000-385 Porto, Portugal (large concert hall with multiple rooms/spaces, including 'Sala Principal' and 'Coliseu Box', per the venue's own GraphQL API data)

identity.notes: https://www.coliseu.pt was provided as the known official website in this task, and this investigation independently re-confirmed it from its own retained evidence: the retained home-page HTML's own <title> is 'Coliseu Porto Ageas' and its meta description names 'O Coliseu Porto' with a stated 75-year history matching the well-known real venue. The GraphQL backend host (nest.coliseu.pt) is a same-registrable-domain subdomain referenced directly and only by this official site's own first-party /env-config.js (not discovered via a third party or search engine) — and its own data is self-referential: one sampled event (id 1911, 'PROMENADE 2026') lists its own `promoter.name` as literally 'Coliseu Porto Ageas'. DISCREPANCY WITH THE OLDER, LOOSE sources/porto.json NOTE (not silently carried forward): that note recorded acquisition_method: 'UNKNOWN' with acquisition_path_detail concluding 'No server-rendered listing or JSON/JSON-LD was found within this bounded search. Would require a headless-browser collector family this project has not built.' This investigation's own Level 1 re-fetch reproduces that shell finding exactly (still true), but its Level 2 escalation — which the older note explicitly did not attempt ('not attempted further tonight') — found a genuine public JSON API. The old note is recorded here as superseded by this investigation's own deeper, independently retained evidence, not silently assumed correct or silently overwritten (sources/porto.json itself was never touched by this investigation, per policy).

site_classification.platform: Front end: a React single-page app served as a static, fully client-rendered bundle (create-react-app-style webpack chunks: /static/js/2.*.chunk.js, main.*.chunk.js), with React Router client-side routes including /agenda and /evento/:slug (confirmed present verbatim in the retained main bundle). Backend: a separate, publicly-hosted GraphQL API (Apollo/GraphQL server fingerprints — 'apollographql'/'apollodata' strings — found in the retained vendor JS bundle; server itself is Express-powered per its own X-Powered-By header) at https://nest.coliseu.pt/graph/, with introspection enabled and CORS fully open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). This is a client-rendered SPA whose own frontend publicly discloses a genuine, queryable public JSON (GraphQL) API — distinct from a plain CLIENT_RENDERED site with no discoverable data path.

data_paths.kind: HTML_EVENT_LIST_PAGE (client-rendered shell only — REJECTED as a direct data path)
HTML_EVENT_DETAIL_ROUTE (client-rendered shell; URL pattern confirmed to resolve, but detail data itself comes from the GraphQL API above, not this route's own HTML)

title.notes: The GraphQL Event type's `name` field is reliably present on every sampled event (e.g. 'He´s Back | Michael Jackson Tribute', 'Sigur Rós - The Orchestral Tour', 'Bruna Louise: Novo Show', 'PROMENADE 2026 - Os Prelúdios de Liszt', 'PRIMEIRA BOX apresenta: Ed + João Não & Lil Noon + Rodrigo 13'), non-null (NON_NULL String per the introspected schema) for 5/5 sampled events. Left null here (a general capability finding across the sample, not one single event) — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the per-event values.

start_date.notes: The GraphQL Event type's `startDate` field (schema type DateTime, NON_NULL) is a genuine UTC ISO-8601 instant ending in 'Z' for all 5 sampled events (e.g. '2026-09-12T20:00:00.000Z'), not merely a floating local datetime — a stronger guarantee than several prior investigations in this repository have found. No ambiguity about date-vs-time-only was observed.

time.notes: The time-of-day portion of the same `startDate` UTC instant (e.g. '20:00:00.000Z'). Same evidence as start_date.

end.notes: The Event type exposes `estimatedDuration` (a NON_NULL Float, observed in seconds — e.g. 8100 = 2.25h for the Michael Jackson tribute show), which the offline-proof script mechanically combines with startDate to derive an approximate end instant. This is deliberately NOT marked PROVEN: the field is explicitly named 'estimated' by the source itself, not an authoritative scheduled/confirmed end time, so promoting a derived value to a precise claimed 'end' would overstate what the source actually guarantees. A future collector may use it as a best-effort approximate end, clearly labelled as such.

venue_location.notes: The Event type's `room` field (Room object: id/name only, per introspection) gives a named space within the already-identified venue for every sampled event ('Sala Principal' for 4/5 sampled events, 'Coliseu Box' for 1/5). The Room type itself carries no independent street address or coordinates — venue_location resolves to 'this named room, within Coliseu Porto Ageas' rather than a separately-geocoded address; the venue's own physical address is not exposed by this API at all (it lives only in this repository's own venues/manual-coordinates registry, which this investigation did not touch).

source_record_id.notes: The Event type's `id` field (schema type ID, NON_NULL) was proven empirically stable: for 2 of the 5 sampled events, independently re-querying the exact same event via a completely separate query path (`eventBySlug(slug: ...)` instead of the `events` list query) reproduced the identical id both times (1951/1951 and 1923/1923 — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 7). This satisfies the stable-identifier rule via empirical proof (repeated acquisition of the same record via two different paths returning the same id). No multi-occurrence/multi-session id-sharing ambiguity (of the kind found in the gulbenkian-lisbon-01 investigation) was observed in this bounded sample, though this investigation did not specifically search for a recurring/multi-date production to stress-test that edge case — a future, larger sample should re-check this.

event_url.notes: A public, canonical-looking event detail URL is deterministically constructible as https://www.coliseu.pt/evento/{slug}, where {slug} is the API's own `slug` field (e.g. '20260912-he-s-back-michael-jackson-tribute'). The React route pattern '/evento/:slug' was found verbatim, byte-for-byte, in the retained main JS bundle (not guessed), and a direct curl GET of that constructed URL for one sampled event resolved 200 OK (not a 404), confirming the server recognises the route. The resulting page is itself only the same empty client-rendered shell (the actual event content still comes from the GraphQL API, not this HTML), which is recorded honestly rather than implied to be a server-rendered detail page.

price.notes: No price, cost, or ticket-price field exists anywhere on the Event type, nor anywhere in the full 179-type GraphQL schema (mechanically confirmed by grepping the retained full schema-type-list evidence for any price/cost-named type — none found). The Event type does expose `ticketsSeller` (e.g. 'TICKETLINE', 'BLUETICKET') and `ticketsUrl` pointing to a third-party ticketing site, where price presumably is shown — but that is a separate third-party page this investigation did not fetch, and using a third-party ticketing site as first-party price authority is exactly the kind of use this policy's 'Third-party sources' section says must be explicitly governed elsewhere, not assumed here.

blockers.description: `ticketsUrl` is not consistently a full absolute URL across sampled events: 3/5 sampled events returned a bare relative slug/path fragment (e.g. 'sigur-ros-102947', or a session-specific fragment like 'he-s-back-michael-jackson-tribute-104399/sessao/125992_16_1789243200'), while 2/5 returned a complete https:// URL to a different domain (bol.pt). A collector must combine `ticketsSeller` with `ticketsUrl` using seller-specific URL-construction rules (not yet reverse-engineered here), rather than assuming ticketsUrl is always directly usable as-is.

`estimatedDuration` is explicitly source-labelled as an estimate, not an authoritative end time — a collector deriving `end` from startDate + estimatedDuration must propagate that this is an approximation, never present it as a confirmed venue-scheduled end.

GraphQL introspection being enabled in production is itself notable (many production APIs disable it) — a future collector should not assume this stays enabled indefinitely, and should have a fallback of hand-written queries (already captured in this investigation's evidence) if introspection is later disabled.

This investigation's bounded 5-event sample happened not to include any multi-date/recurring production sharing one id across dates (the pattern found at gulbenkian-lisbon-01). A larger future sample should specifically check whether Coliseu's API has the same subEvent-style id-sharing edge case before fully trusting source_record_id as always 1:1 with a single performance instance.

reasons: identity.status is PROVEN at HIGH confidence: the known official URL's own retained HTML title/meta match the well-known real venue, and the discovered GraphQL API host is a same-registrable-domain, first-party-referenced subdomain whose own data is self-referential (a promoter literally named 'Coliseu Porto Ageas').
site_classification.acquisition_class is PUBLIC_JSON_API, a resolved/supported class — a live, public, CORS-open, introspectable GraphQL endpoint was independently discovered and queried.
The GraphQL endpoint data_paths entry is access:PUBLIC and status:CONFIRMED against retained evidence (multiple successful, bounded, read-only queries).
field_assessment.title.state and field_assessment.start_date.state are both PROVEN (start_date is a genuine UTC ISO instant, not merely floating-local).

field_assessment.source_record_id.state is PROVEN under the stable-identifier rule, empirically demonstrated: the same id reproduced identically across two independent query paths for 2/2 cross-checked events.
collector_assessment.recommended_family is JSON_API, a known collector family, at HIGH confidence.

evidence/offline-proof.mjs + evidence/offline-proof-output.txt provide a DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item: a dependency-free, no-network re-parse of every retained fixture that mechanically reproduces every claim above (shell-emptiness, env-config API discovery, schema introspection, sample-field presence, id-stability cross-check, and event_url route resolution).

collector_assessment.blockers contains only MINOR entries (ticketsUrl format inconsistency, estimatedDuration being approximate-only, introspection-availability fragility, and an unverified multi-date-id edge case) — none CRITICAL.

This investigation used only ordinary, read-only, unauthenticated GraphQL-over-HTTP requests to a publicly CORS-open endpoint already referenced by the site's own public client code — no CAPTCHA/login/paywall was encountered or bypassed, no mutation was ever sent, and no private/undocumented API was assumed (the endpoint documents its own protocol in its own error message and supports standard introspection).

This decision independently supersedes, in effect, the older loose sources/porto.json note describing this candidate as requiring a headless-browser collector — that note's own Level 1 finding (empty shell) is still correct and was independently re-confirmed here, but its conclusion stopped at Level 1 and never attempted the Level 2 structural escalation that this investigation completed. Per policy, this investigation.json is the authoritative research conclusion, but it does NOT itself edit sources/*.json or any registry.
